reference.source: Sperling Pediatric Endocrinology / Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guidelines
clinicalPearls: A rare cause of primary adrenal insufficiency; the classic X-linked form results from mutations in the NR0B1 gene encoding the nuclear receptor DAX1

It typically presents in male infants with a salt-wasting adrenal crisis (hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia, hypoglycaemia and hypotension) or with more insidious glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid deficiency in childhood
It is characteristically combined with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, which becomes apparent as absent or arrested puberty
Because it is X-linked, affected individuals are usually boys with carrier mothers, and a family history of infant deaths or adrenal insufficiency may be present
It is distinguished from congenital adrenal hyperplasia by the absence of a steroidogenic enzyme block and virilisation and by low gonadotropins
Management is lifelong glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement, with induction of puberty and fertility issues addressed later
Contiguous gene deletions at Xp21 can associate it with Duchenne muscular dystrophy and glycerol kinase deficiency
reference.pathophysiology: DAX1, encoded by NR0B1, is a nuclear receptor essential for development of the adrenal cortex and of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis. Loss-of-function mutations impair formation of the definitive adrenal cortex, producing primary adrenal insufficiency with deficient cortisol and aldosterone, and disrupt gonadotropin secretion and gonadal function, causing hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Impaired spermatogenesis tends to persist even with gonadotropin therapy, reflecting a combined central and gonadal defect.
additionalDifferentials: Other causes of primary adrenal insufficiency such as adrenoleukodystrophy or autoimmune adrenalitis
ACTH resistance syndromes and familial glucocorticoid deficiency
Adrenal hypoplasia from steroidogenic factor-1 (NR5A1/SF1) defects
Isolated hypogonadotropic hypogonadism such as Kallmann syndrome
additionalInvestigations: Serum electrolytes and glucose with paired cortisol and ACTH, expected to show low cortisol and high ACTH in primary failure
Plasma renin and aldosterone to confirm mineralocorticoid deficiency
ACTH (Synacthen) stimulation test showing an impaired cortisol response
Gonadotropins (LH and FSH) and sex steroids, expected to be low in hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
17-hydroxyprogesterone and a steroid profile to exclude congenital adrenal hyperplasia
NR0B1 (DAX1) genetic testing and evaluation for contiguous Xp21 gene deletions
Adrenal imaging where structural assessment is needed
redFlags: A salt-wasting adrenal crisis in a male infant requiring emergency treatment
A family history of infant deaths or X-linked adrenal disease
Failure to enter or progress through puberty
Features suggesting a contiguous gene syndrome such as muscular dystrophy or developmental delay
reference.prognosis: With early diagnosis and lifelong hormone replacement the outlook is good, but survival depends on prompt recognition and treatment of adrenal crises; fertility is usually impaired despite treatment, and associated gene deletions worsen the prognosis.
pitfalls: Misdiagnosing it as congenital adrenal hyperplasia and missing the correct genetic cause
Failing to anticipate pubertal failure and delaying induction of puberty
Under-recognising precipitants of adrenal crisis and giving inadequate sick-day dosing
Overlooking an associated Xp21 contiguous gene deletion syndrome
management: Provide lifelong glucocorticoid replacement with hydrocortisone for cortisol deficiency
Give mineralocorticoid replacement with fludrocortisone and salt supplementation for aldosterone deficiency
Treat salt-wasting adrenal crisis promptly with parenteral hydrocortisone, intravenous fluids and glucose, and correction of hyperkalaemia and hypoglycaemia
Educate on sick-day dosing and provide an emergency steroid card and injectable hydrocortisone
Induce and maintain puberty with testosterone replacement for the associated hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
Counsel on impaired fertility that often persists despite gonadotropin therapy and discuss assisted reproduction
Offer genetic counselling for X-linked NR0B1 inheritance, test carrier mothers and evaluate for contiguous Xp21 gene deletions
